messages:
Maya: FYI - hit a weird tokenization/merge regression on the new quantized bring-up (rdx-11b-q4). CJK <> RTL boundary tokens are getting concatenated across scripts.
Josh: ugh. can you paste an example? :eyes:
Maya: Sure. Running a small multilingual translation eval (JP/EN + AR/EN) — before quant we saw normal splits. After q4 quantize: 
```
src (mixed): 中国とالعالم
tokenized (fp16): ["中", "国", "と", "العالم"]
tokenized (q4): ["中国الع", "الم"]
```
So the Arabic word got partially merged into the preceding Chinese token, which breaks decoder alignment and harms translation quality.
Priya: That looks like a vocab/index mismatch rather than tokenizer algorithm change. Did the quant pipeline re-save the model with a different tokenizer metadata? Any hash mismatch on vocab.json?
Maya: Checked hashes: model.vocab hash == expected. But the runtime compiles a fused tokenization kernel for speed on the quant binary. Variant: rdx-runtime-prod-1.2.3 uses a new bytes->codepoint fastpath that doesn't normalize ZWNJ/ZWJ and merges adjacent byte sequences in one buffer write. Repro on CPU quantized runtime too.
Eric: Interesting. What metrics are we seeing? chrF / BLEU drop?
Maya: Small eval snippet: on en-zh/jp-en combined testset, BLEU dropped from 28.4 -> 26.1, chrF from 54.2 -> 50.9. AR-EN dev set BLEU 31.0 -> 27.2. Token-level alignment errors spiked 4x.
Josh: Oof. Could be an encoding boundary bug: our tokenizer expects Unicode-normalized input (NFKC) but fastpath was skipping normalization to save cycles.
Maya: Exactly. I logged raw bytes in the q4 runtime: we see no NFKC normalizer call in fastpath. Patch idea: add a lightweight normalization step on script boundaries only.
Priya: Do we have a quick mitigation? Hotfix for Hosted API while we patch runtime?
Maya: Two mitigation options: 1) roll back runtime to rdx-runtime-prod-1.2.2 (safe, costs perf) 2) apply request pre-normalization in the ingestion layer (cheap CPU, per-request cost). For Hosted we can enable pre-normalize on the model route config.
Eric: Can you put a config flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in? Also need a test that covers mixed-script boundaries in our eval harness.
Maya: I've added a new unit test in the eval harness: samples/edgecases/mixed_script_boundaries.tsv (JP+AR+CJK+LTR). Running now, PR incoming.
Josh: Put the metrics in the thread and tag infra. Also drop a small reproducer script so SRE can run on prod nodes.
Maya: Reproducer inlined below: 
```bash
python -c "from tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer('rdx-vocab.json'); print(t.encode('中国とالعالم'))"
```
On q4 runtime this prints the merged sequence.
deploy-bot: deploy log: canary deploy rdx-runtime-prod-1.2.3 -> group infra-ml-2 at 2026-01-15T09:10:12Z. :information_source:
Priya: OK I'm going to enable pre-normalize for the hosted model route as a temporary fix. Will monitor latency. Maya - can you open a rollback/patch ticket?
Maya: Opening ticket now: INF-1129. Title: "Tokenization fastpath: normalization skip causes cross-script merges in q4 runtime". Assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml. Description includes reproducer, metrics, suggested mitigation.
Eric: For Dedicated/private customers, we should ship a runtime patch (1.2.4) that reintroduces normalization but keeps fastpath heuristics. Devs in eng-runtime - ping for ETA.
Josh: Also add an eval that quantizes with both rdx-11b-q4 and rdx-11b-fp16 and compares tokenization outputs. Want to avoid silent regressions in future.
Maya: Agreed. I'll add a regression test to the quant CI that runs the mixed-script sample and checks token boundaries. Will also add a Canary metric: "script-boundary-token-merges" to console.
Priya: Thanks. Quick note: users reported a few support tickets showing Arabic text appended to Chinese product names in logs — likely same root cause. I'll flag support so they can triage incoming tickets as related.
Josh: Nice catch. :thumbsup: Keep us posted on the rollback decision.
Maya: Will do. Planning to enable pre-normalize in hosted tonight and open rollback if latency impact > 5%.
